summary: "What Happens Up There" is an interactive digital storybook website that tells the stories of NASA’s robotic space exploration objects on the Moon and Mars through character development, pop-up book visuals, audio, and gamification. Designed for children ages 8–12, the project aims to simplify NASA’s complex space mission archives into an educational, interactive, and emotionally engaging learning experience. Each character represents a real object, such as a rover, lander, or other exploration vehicle, with a personality and backstory based on its actual function, achievements, and mission history. Through minigames inspired by each object’s functions and mission facts, users learn about their contributions to the history of space exploration. With the theme “Abandoned but Not Forgotten,” the project reframes neglect as a way to preserve the stories of objects that have completed their missions, pioneered exploration, or lost communication—but still have a place in the history of human exploration. Drawing on the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), What Happens Up There combines scientific accuracy, accessible education, and emotional storytelling to bring forgotten stories back to life.
details:
1. Project Overview & How It Works

What Happens Up There is an interactive storybook website that transforms NASA's technical mission records about exploration equipment on Mars and the Moon into engaging learning experiences for children aged 8–12.

Users begin by selecting a spacecraft character and exploring its profile through interactive 3D models, mission facts, and story excerpts. They then follow its journey through narrated storytelling, character dialogues, and interactive scenes. Throughout the story, users encounter minigames inspired by the actual functions and operating principles of the featured equipment, allowing them to understand scientific concepts through purposeful interaction rather than passive reading.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

The project aims to make complex space exploration information more accessible and enjoyable for younger audiences. Its intended impact includes:

  • For Children: Encouraging curiosity about space exploration, strengthening scientific interest, and introducing mission histories through interactive learning.
  • For Parents and Educators: Providing an accessible, fact-based learning resource that can support individual or shared educational experiences.
  • For the Wider Community: Demonstrating an alternative approach to presenting NASA's public documentation through storytelling and interactive media, with potential for expansion to other missions and topics.

3. Technology & Implementation

The project was developed as a browser-based website using:

  • React & Vite: Frontend development and application foundation.
  • React Three Fiber & Three.js: Interactive 3D models and WebGL rendering.
  • GSAP & Motion: Animations, transitions, and interface interactions.
  • Zustand: Application state management and user progression.
  • Howler.js: Audio playback for narration, character dialogue, and sound effects.

4. Creativity & Innovation

The project's creativity lies in transforming spacecraft into story characters, rather than presenting them merely as technical equipment. Inspired by the theme "Abandoned but Not Forgotten," it reframes the end of a spacecraft's operational life as an opportunity to preserve and retell its journey and contributions to space exploration. The experience combines digital pop-up book-inspired visuals, audio storytelling, interactive 3D elements, and fact-based gamification. Each minigame is directly connected to the featured equipment's real functions or mission activities, making interaction part of the learning process rather than merely an entertainment feature.

5. Development Considerations

Throughout development, the team considered several factors to ensure the experience remained engaging, accessible, and scientifically grounded:

  • Target Audience: Adapting language, storytelling, interactions, and game complexity to children aged 8–12.
  • Scientific Accuracy: Using NASA's official mission records, particularly the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), as the foundation for character development and gameplay. Creative interpretations are kept distinct from verified mission facts.
  • Learning Experience: Ensuring that every interaction reinforces a relevant scientific concept or mission fact.
  • Accessibility & Performance: Choosing a browser-based platform without requiring dedicated app installation, while considering 3D rendering efficiency, asset management, and responsive interactions.
  • Creative & Technical Consistency: Maintaining coherence between character identities, visual assets, narration, and gameplay.

AI-assisted tools were also used to support coding, debugging, creative asset production, and documentation. All generated outputs and suggestions were reviewed by the team before implementation.
